fair_value_policy: Fair Value V2.1 is the sole valuation baseline. Semantic scores in this file must not directly overwrite official numeric macro series or Fair Value.

events.observed_evidence: Reuters reported on September 14 that a scheduled Oman meeting between Iran and Gulf Arab states on reopening the Strait of Hormuz was postponed. With the Saudi East-West Pipeline still shut and fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia and Gulf shipping, Brent futures rose to about $107.84/bbl and WTI to about $102.85/bbl in early Asian trade.
events.semantic_interpretation: The postponement removes a near-term diplomatic de-escalation catalyst while physical supply and chokepoint constraints remain active. The additional oil-price rise is market confirmation of a persistent delivered-energy risk rather than an official production statistic.

events.observed_evidence: Reuters reported that repeated Ukrainian long-range drone attacks on Russian refineries have reduced Russian fuel production and contributed to shortages. U.S. President Donald Trump publicly urged Ukraine to stop targeting Russian diesel infrastructure. Reuters also reported that Russia downgraded its 2026 oil-output forecast to a 17-year low and revised its 2026-2027 fuel-export outlook because of the war.
events.semantic_interpretation: Russia-Ukraine energy-infrastructure attacks are now a separate refined-product supply shock that can reinforce the Middle East crude shock. The main Taiwan transmission is through global diesel/freight costs, inflation expectations, rates and external demand rather than a direct Taiwan security channel.

notes: Observed evidence is separated from semantic interpretation. Market prices and Reuters-reported supply impacts in this file are semantic/research observations and must not overwrite official deterministic macro or production series.
